title: Shift-maximum equality for periodic nonlinear complexity
summary: Determine whether the source's added-term threshold forces an exact maximum nonlinear complexity over all circular shifts of a representative sequence.

formal_statement.body: Let $s_n\in R(n,c,d)$ be an aperiodic representative binary sequence with $c\ge\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ and $\operatorname{add}(s_n)=t$. If $t>n-c-d$, must $$\max_{0\le i<n}\operatorname{nlc}(R_i(s_n))=n-d?$$ Prove the implication for every admissible $(n,c,d,t,s_n)$, or give a fully specified counterexample satisfying all source definitions and parameter constraints.

scope.domain: Periodic binary sequences and nonlinear feedback shift-register complexity
assumptions: $s_n$ is aperiodic and belongs to the source-defined set $R(n,c,d)$
$R_i$ is the right circular shift and $\operatorname{nlc}$ is minimum NFSR length
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source verifies the equality numerically only for n <= 30. Later structure and enumeration results for high nonlinear complexity do not prove the implication or provide a counterexample.

progress.summary: The source states Open Problem 1 after numerical verification through n = 30 and explains that its existing technique cannot prove or disprove the equality.
